Transition Metal-Catalyzed Benzannulation towards
Naturally Occurring Carbazole Alkaloids
Xue Zhang[a] and Shengming Ma[a, b]
Abstract: In this account, we will summarize our recent
progress on development of Pt- or Au-catalyzed benzannula-
tion of 1-indolyl-2,3-allenols for the efficient construction of
carbazole skeleton via a metal carbene intermediate and its
application towards the synthesis of naturally occurring
carbazole alkaloids. The strategy enjoys the outstanding
regioselectivity, atom economy, mild reaction conditions,
substrate scope, functional group tolerance.
Keywords: Gold-catalysis · Benzannulation · Carbazole alkaloids · Metal carbenes · Total synthesis
1. Introduction
Carbazole alkaloids have received increasing attention as an
important class of heteroaromatic compounds due to their
unique biological and pharmacological activities, as well as
their exceptional thermal, electrical, and optical properties. [1]
During the last four decades, an increasing number of
naturally occurring carbazole alkaloids have been isolated
from different natural sources, among which the taxonomi-
cally similar plants of the genus Murraya, Glycosmis,
Clausena and Micromelum from the family Rutaceae represent
the richest sources. [2] Their pharmacological effects are very
broad, including anti-HIV ,anti-TB, anti-malarial, anti-tumor,
and neuronal cell protective activity.[1]
The biologically active carbazole alkaloids call for the
diversity of compounds with such a core structure. Thus, many
synthetic approaches have been developed. [3] The method-
ologies that have been often utilized for the construction of
carbazoles skeleton are summarized as follows: the Fischer-
Borsche synthesis is one of the classical procedures for
carbazole alkaloids (Scheme 1a);
[4] condensation of cyclo-
hexanone with phenylhydrazines affords the arylhydrazones,
which could cyclize to afford the indole unit through Fischer-
Borsche cyclization. Then, dehydrogenation of the tetrahydro-
carbazoles produces carbazoles finally by using palladium on
activated carbon or chloranil (Scheme 1a); another widely
used method for carbazole synthesis is the deoxygenative
cyclization of o-nitrobiphenyls in triethyl phosphite under
reflux, which is also known as Cadogan synthesis (Sche-
me 1b).
[5] 1-Phenylbenzotriazole, prepared by diazotization of
N-(2-aminophenyl)aniline, would transform to carbazole under
thermal reaction conditions, which is called Graebe-Ullmann
synthesis (Scheme 1c).[6] Kno¨lker et al. reported iron-mediated
carbazole synthesis protocol (Scheme 1d): [7] The electrophilic
aromatic substitution of arylamines by the tricarbonyl iron-
coordinated cyclohexadienylium ions affords an arylamine-
substituted tricarbonyl(h
4-cyclohexadiene)iron complex, which
would lead to a carbazole by oxidative cyclization; cyclo-
dehydrogenation of diarylamines is another practical method
for the synthesis of carbazoles. Diarylamines can be obtained
directly by palladium(0)-catalyzed Buchwald-Hartwig cou-
pling of aryl halides with arylamines (Scheme 1e).
[8] Similarly,
carbazoles may also be synthesized via 2-fold palladium(0)-
catalyzed Buchwald-Hartwig coupling of biphenyl-2,2 ’-diyl
bistriflates (or 2,2 ’-dihalobiphenyls) with primary amines
(Scheme 1f);[9] Witulski et al. reported a creative approach for
carbazole synthesis by employing a rhodium-catalyzed [2 +
2 +2] cyclotrimerization of a diyne and an alkyne as the key
step (Scheme 1g).[10]
The above mentioned synthetic strategies for carbazoles
are mostly based on construction of the central pyrrole ring by
cyclization of either diarylamines or biphenyls with an ortho-
nitrogen substituent. Forming a benzene ring to indole via
electrocyclic reaction is another effective strategy for
carbazole construction. The wide availability of indole
derivatives makes this strategy quite practical. A large number
of carbazole derivatives have been prepared efficiently by
electrocyclic reaction of 2,3-divinylindoles at high temperature
in the presence of dehydrogenating agents such as Pd/C or
DDQ (Scheme 2a).
[11] An improvement of this electrocyclic
procedure is cyclization of 2,3-difunctionalized indole via an
allene intermediate (Scheme 2b).
[12] A further indole benzan-
nulation of 3-(buta-1,3-dienyl)indoles has been applied to the
synthesis of 3-oxygenated carbazoles (Scheme 2c). [13] In
addition to the methods described above, there are still some
alternative protocols.[3]
Although numerous effective synthetic approaches for the
construction of carbazole framework have been developed,
there remain some limitations, [3] such as low yields, harsh

[15] Due to the easy availability of the starting

(indol-2-yl)-2,3-allenols provides a general route to differently
substituted carbazoles. In this account, we will summarize the

naturally occurring carbazole alkaloids.
2. Reaction Development
2.1 [PtCl2]-Catalyzed Cyclization of 1-(Indol-2-yl)-2,3-allenols
Intrigued by our previous observation of PtCl 4-catalyzed
intermolecular cyclization reaction of indoles with b-allenols,
which afforded indole derivatives with a saturated 6-mem-
bered cyclic ether at the C3-position (Scheme 3), [16] we
envisioned that polycyclic products 2 would be obtained if 1-
(indol-2-yl)-2,3-allenols 1 undergo a similar reaction. How-
ever, carbazoles 3 were formed unexpectedly at room temper-
ature (Scheme 3). The starting materials are easily available
from the related 1 H-indole-2-carbaldehydes based on known
methods.[17] After careful screening of the reaction parameters,
the standard reaction conditions are defined as follows: the
reaction of 1-(indol-2-yl)-2,3-allenols 1 was conducted with
5 mol % PtCl 2 in toluene at room temperature. This trans-
formation is quite general with a very good functional group
tolerance. Some typical results are listed in Table 1.[14]
A possible mechanism involving a 1,2-H migration of the
Pt-carbene intermediate was proposed for this transformation.
In addition, 4,4-carbon disubstitution was introduced to the 1-
(indol-2-yl)-2,3-allenols to further check the intermediacy of
the Pt-carbene intermediate and the selectivity of the sub-
sequent carbon-carbon single bond cleavage via 1,2-carbon
migration for formation of 3A or 3B (Scheme 4).
[18]
After some trials, we achieved a highly selective carbon-
carbon single bond cleavage reaction of 4-aryl-4-alkyl-
substitued allenols. Different carbazoles were provided in
moderate to good yields with the aromatic group migration
exclusively. Further introduction of different substituents to
the original indole substrate shows that this protocol provides
an efficient approach to assemble the substituents to any
location of carbazole skeleton (Scheme 5).
[18]
2.2 [AuCl]-Catalyzed Cyclization of 1-(Indol-2-yl)-2,3-allenols
For the purpose of synthesizing the naturally occurring carbazole,
a methoxy group has been introduced to the 2-position of the
starting 1-(indol-2-yl)-2,3-allenols. We observed that AuCl is a
much more effective catalyst than PtCl
2.[15] In the total synthesis
of siamenol, we utilized this transformation as the key step for
constructing the carbazole skeleton from the required methoxy-
substituted allenol1a. Under the standard reaction conditions,
[14]
the PtCl2-catalyzed cyclization of1a provided carbzaole3a in a
relatively low yield (61 %), probably due to the existence of
methoxy group. However, when AuCl was used as the catalyst,
3a was produced in a much higher yield (81 %), exclusively
(Equation 1).

2.3 [IPrAuCl]/AgSbF6-Catalyzed Cyclization of
4-benzoxyl-1-(indol-2-yl)-2-alkynols
In 2014, another efficient procedure for carbazole framework
construction from indoles is developed by our group. [20]
[IPrAuCl]/AgSbF6-catalyzed cyclization of 4-benzoxyl-1-(in-
dol-2-yl)-2-alkynols 4 occurred smoothly in 1,2-dichloro-
ethane (DCE) in the presence of 4 A˚ MS, producing a series of
differently poly-substituted 2-oxygenated carbazole derivatives
in good yields under very mild conditions (Table 3). The
reaction was proven to be quite broad in substrate scope
(Table 3).[20] Highly selective migration is also observed in this
transformation: compared with methyl group (R 3), propyl, 4-
methylphenyl, and 4-chlorophenyl groups (R 4) all migrates
exclusively (Table 3, entries 10–13). Particularly, the starting
materials are readily available from the reaction of indole-
carbaldehydes with the related terminal alkynes. With this
protocol, poly-substituted carbazols could be obtained by
assembling substituents to the phenyl ring, the N-atom of the
indole unit, and the 1-position and two 4-positions of the
alkynols.
A plausible mechanism is proposed based on the deute-
rium-labelling experiment (Scheme 7).
[20] The benzoate unit in
substrate 4 undergoes 1,3-migration, via the nucleophilic
attack of the carbonyl oxygen on the Au + -coordinated C/C0C
triple bond, generating the allene intermediate IM6. 6-Endo-
trig-type nucleophilic attack of the indolyl C3 at the
coordinated C=C bond in the allene moity would generate the
vinyl/C0gold species IM7. Subsequent elimination of H 2O
affords a gold-carbene intermediate IM8. The final 1,2-R 4
(R4 = H, aryl, and alkyl) migration of IM8 would produce the
2-oxygenated carbazoles 5 with regeneration of the gold
catalyst (Scheme 7).

By retrosynthetic analysis, the Au-catalyzed cyclization of
1-indoly-2-methoxy-2,3-allenols is the key step (Scheme 9). [15]
Readily available methoxypropadiene [24] and indole-2-carbal-
dehyde are chosen as the starting materials for the synthesis of
these starting indoly-2,3-allenols.[17]
3.1.1 Total Synthesis of Siamenol
The required methoxy-substituted allenol 1a may be synthe-
sized conveniently from the addition of 1-methoxypropa-1,2-
dienyl lithium
[24] to 1-benzyl-5-methylindole-2-carbaldehyde
6a. Subsequently, AuCl-catalyzed cyclization of 1a under the
standard reaction conditions afforded carbzaole 3a exclusively
in a good yield. Regioselective electrophilic bromination of
1a at C-3 with NBS provided 7a . The following debenzyla-
tion using potassium tert-butoxide/DMSO under oxygen
atmosphere[25] produced 8a. Then, 9a would be formed by the
demethylation of 8a with BBr 3 in CH 2Cl2.[26] When we used
acetate as the protection form of the free OH group ( 10 a),
siamenol was eventually obtained via the coupling and instant
deprotection in one-pot (Scheme 10). [15] Total synthesis of
siamenol from methoxypropadiene is 7 steps with 21 % overall
yield.
3.1.2 Total Synthesis of Isomukonidine, Clausine L,
Mukonidine, Glycosinine, and Mukonal
From 1-benzyl-1H-indole-2-carbaldehyde 6b , a similar ap-
proach may also be used for the synthesis of carbazole 8b.
Starting from 8b, isomukonidine was obtained by Br /C0Li
exchange with n-BuLi and the subsequent carboxylation with
CO2; clausine L was provided by esterification of the
carboxylic acid functionality in isomukonidine with MeI;
mukonidine was synthesized by removal of the methyl group
in the methoxy group in clausine L by treatment with BBr
3 in
CH2Cl2;[26] glycosinine was generated by deprotonation of 8b
with KH, Li /C0Br exchange, and addition of dimethylforma-
mide; mukonal was afforded by demethylation of glycosinine
by treatment with BBr3 in CH2Cl2 (Scheme 11). The net results
for the total synthesises of these carbazole alkaloids from
methoxypropadiene are: isomukonidine (5 steps with 29 %
overall yield), clausine L (6 steps with 26 % overall yield),
mukonidine (7 steps with 17 % overall yield), glycosinine (5
steps with 34 % overall yield), and mukonal (6 steps with 30 %
overall yield).
[21]
3.1.3 Total Synthesis of Clausine V
A similar approach was also used for the synthesis of allenol
1c , which underwent the AuCl-catalyzed cyclization smoothly
under the standard reaction conditions to afford carbazole 3c ,
exclusively. Clausine V was provided by debenzylation with
potassium tert-butoxide/DMSO under oxygen atmosphere
(Scheme 12). Total synthesis of clausine V from methoxypro-
padiene took 3 steps with 61 % overall yield.[21]

Clauszoline-K, Clauszoline-L, Clausine-M, and Clausine-N

In 2013, karapinchamie A with a N-geranyl substituent[29] was
isolated from Murraya Koenigii , which is a used as herb
medicine in southern Asia, and showed useful melanogenesis
inhibitory activity. [IPrAuCl]/AgSbF

benzoxyl-1-(indol-2-yl)-2-alkynols has a major advantage of
its diversity, which allows even the N-substituent. Thus, the
first total synthesis of karapinchamine A was executed by
using the reaction presented in Table 3 as the key step.[20]
The commercially available ethyl 5-methyl-1H-indole-2-
carboxylate 19 was treated with (2 E)-geranyl bromide to
introduce the geranyl group to the nitrogen atom. Subsequent
reduction with LiAlH
4 and oxidation with MnO 2 afforded
indole-carbaldehyde 22. Then the reaction of 22 with (3-
(benzoyloxy)prop-1-yn-1-yl)lithium provided the required
propargylic alcohol 4a in 83 % yield conveniently. Under the
catalysis of [IPrAuCl]/AgSbF

4. Conclusion and Perspectives
In this account, we summarized our recent progress achieved
in the studies of Au-catalyzed benzannulation and its
application towards the synthesis of naturally occurring
carbazole alkaloids. Due to the outstanding regioselectivity,
atom economy, mild reaction conditions, scope, and functional
group tolerance, these Au-catalyzed reactions would provide
an efficient access to the related natural products and
unnatural products, which will be of interest to medicinal
chemists. Further investigations including biological activity
studies and other carbazole alkaloids synthesis are still being
carried out in our laboratory.
